stemMd: Citizenship of the European Union - held today by every national of a member state, alongside national citizenship - was first established by which treaty?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** This is citizenship of the *Union*, and a citizenship of the Union cannot be older than the Union itself. So ask first which treaty created the European Union.

**The fact that settles it.** The Maastricht Treaty - formally the Treaty on European Union, signed on 7 February 1992 and in force from 1 November 1993 - created the European Union and, with it, citizenship of the Union. It gave every national of a member state the right to move and reside freely within the Union, to vote and stand as a candidate in municipal and European Parliament elections in the member state where they live, to consular protection from other member states' embassies abroad, and to petition the European Parliament.

**How to check it.** Put the five texts in order: Treaty of Rome 1957, Schengen Agreement 1985, Maastricht 1992, Nice 2001, Lisbon 2007. The two earlier texts predate the Union; the two later treaties amended a Union - and a citizenship - that already existed.

distractorRationale.b: The Treaty of Rome (1957) founded the European Economic Community and provided for the free movement of workers. That is an economic right linked to employment, not a citizenship; the Union whose citizenship this is did not exist until 1993.
distractorRationale.a: The Schengen Agreement (1985), first signed by five states at Schengen in Luxembourg, abolished checks at shared internal borders. It concerns borders, not citizenship, and began outside the Community treaties; it was brought into the EU framework only by the Treaty of Amsterdam.
distractorRationale.c: The Treaty of Nice (2001) reformed the institutions to prepare for the enlargement of 2004. By then citizenship of the Union had existed for years; Nice did not create it.
distractorRationale.e: The Treaty of Lisbon (2007) restates that citizenship of the Union is additional to national citizenship and adds rights such as the European citizens' initiative, which makes it a tempting choice. But it built on a citizenship that Maastricht had created fifteen years earlier.

accessibilityText: Question: citizenship of the European Union, held today by every national of a member state alongside national citizenship, was first established by which treaty? The choices are the Schengen Agreement, the Treaty of Rome, the Treaty of Nice, the Maastricht Treaty, and the Treaty of Lisbon.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section (citizenship). The distractors are the other landmark European treaties: two that predate the Union and two that later amended it, including the one that restates citizenship today.

review.author: wave6-polito-til-a-genknow-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The Maastricht Treaty (TEU, 1992/93) created Union citizenship. Rome (1957) came before it, and Nice and Lisbon only amended it. Schengen is not the source of citizenship. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: EU citizenship was created by the Treaty on European Union (Maastricht, 1992, in force 1993). Rome (1957) came before it, and Nice and Lisbon only amended it. Schengen is about border controls.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: citizenship of the Union was introduced by the Treaty on European Union (Maastricht, signed 1992, in force 1993). The Treaty of Rome (1957) and the Schengen Agreement (1985) predate the Union; Nice (2001) and Lisbon (2007) amended treaties under which the citizenship already existed.
